{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q022_colg_crya_remote_homology","answer":"My pretrained understanding is that SCOPe 2.04 treated the ColG collagen-binding domain in 1nqd as a separate fold/superfamily, whereas the later classification recognizes its remote relationship to the Cry3A C-terminal domain in 1dlc within the galactose-binding-domain-like superfamily (b.18.1). They remain different families. This is a proposed common ancestry at superfamily level, stronger than merely sharing an all-beta class or a beta-sandwich fold. I cannot verify the exact old identifiers or the release meant by “current” under the pretrained-only restriction.

The structural argument is correspondence of the beta-sandwich core, including strand connectivity and topology, despite weak sequence similarity. Such detailed correspondence is more informative than a general resemblance between two beta-rich proteins. Nevertheless, structural similarity alone does not prove ancestry, and I cannot supply a verified alignment score or sequence-profile result for this pair.

Their functions are consistent with divergence of an ancestral binding module. The 1nqd domain binds collagen and helps target ColG to its substrate; it is not the enzyme’s proteolytic catalytic domain. Cry3A’s C-terminal domain III contributes to receptor recognition and insect specificity in a multidomain insecticidal toxin. These binding roles provide supporting biological context, but do not establish identical ligand specificity or independently demonstrate homology.

Consequently, the relationship does not justify transferring collagen binding, collagenase activity, insect specificity, or toxicity between the domains. In particular, Cry3A’s pore-forming machinery belongs principally to its N-terminal domain I. Either structure may inform modeling of a conserved ancestral core, but binding loops, ligand contacts, calcium dependence, and domain interactions require separate evidence; a shared superfamily does not make either protein a functionally interchangeable representative.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
